data.gender_notes: Srihari is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Srihari is derived from two Sanskrit words - 'Sri' meaning God and 'Hari' meaning abode. Thus, Srihari means 'God's Abode'. The name Srihari carries the meaning “God's Abode” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada. Parents who choose Srihari usually hope their child will grow to embody god's abode and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Srihari is a devotional name, signifying the belief that God is our eternal abode and refuge.
data.etymology: Srihari belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Abode.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Srihari total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Srihari holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, especially in the traditions of South India. Hari is a popular name for Vishnu, one of the primary deities in Hinduism. Indians have been attaching the prefix 'Sri' to the names of their gods since ancient times as a sign of reverence and respect. Hence, the name Srihari represents Lord Vishnu, who is believed to be the preserver and protector of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeply spiritual level, the name Srihari raises the consciousness of an individual toward the divine. It is a constant reminder of the presence and pervasiveness of God in every sphere of life. The name inspires devotion and surrendering oneself to the divine will, seeking refuge in Lord Vishnu, who is believed to be the eternal abode of peace, happiness, and divinity. The name also symbolizes a inner journey towards attaining a peaceful and pure state of mind.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Srihari, meaning 'Lord of Fortune' or 'God of Wealth', symbolizes the attainment of spiritual wealth and the blessings of the divine within an individual. It is a reminder of the ultimate goal of seeking inner prosperity and happiness above material wealth.
